ai.title: Prompt tweaks for diff generation
ai.summary: Updated prompts in `backend/src/generate-diffs-prompt.ts` and `backend/src/system-prompt.ts` to clarify handling of placeholder comments like `// ... existing code ...`. The diff generation prompt now explicitly expects placeholders in new file content, while the system prompt emphasizes the risk of deleting file content if placeholders are omitted. Internal prompt engineering only.

eli5.text: The assistant that writes code changes for new files now gets clearer instructions about how to handle placeholder comments like "//... existing code...". If it forgets to include these placeholders, the rest of the file content could be accidentally deleted. This is internal prompt engineering only and affects how the diff generation system behaves behind the scenes, not what you directly see or experience today.

ai.title: Restructure manicode as npm package
ai.summary: Reorganizes the monorepo to make the `manicode` CLI an installable npm package. Moves client source files into a new `manicode` workspace, adds `manicode/package.json` and `tsconfig.json`, and updates root `package.json` workspaces. Refactors `backend` and `common` tsconfigs to support composite builds without inheriting from root. Adds `STOP_MARKER` to `backend/src/generate-diffs-prompt.ts`.

eli5.text: The project has been reorganized so the part you interact with can now be installed and run as a standalone tool, rather than only working as a piece of a larger code collection. If you looked, you would see a new self-contained folder for the interactive tool with its own setup files, and the supporting pieces it depends on were adjusted to build correctly independently. A stop signal was also added to one of the backend instructions so automated code edits are told explicitly where to end their response. This is live today as part of the current source.

ai.title: CLI direct write smooths input typing
ai.summary: CLI input handler writes keystrokes directly to stdout instead of full line refresh. `process.stdout.write(key)` replaces `this.refreshLine()` in the character append path. `getInputLineCount` extracted from `refreshLine` to track line height after direct writes. Scope limited to `manicode/src/cli.ts`.

eli5.text: When you type into the assistant's command-line tool, each letter now appears on your screen immediately instead of waiting for the whole line to redraw. This makes typing feel smoother because the tool writes each keystroke directly to the display rather than refreshing the entire line for every character. The change only affects the internal command-line interface used by the development team and is already live in the code.

ai.title: CLI history navigation preserves unsent input
ai.summary: CLI history navigation now preserves the current `inputBuffer` when moving through previous commands. The `savedInput` property stores the active buffer before history traversal begins and restores it when the index returns to -1. This prevents the loss of unsent text when navigating up and down in `manicode/src/cli.ts`. The fix ensures that returning to the end of the history stack displays the original input rather than an empty string.

eli5.text: If you type a partial command in the terminal and then use the Up and Down arrow keys to look through your past commands, your unfinished text is now remembered and restored when you return to the bottom of the list. Previously your partially typed command was erased as soon as you navigated into history. The program now saves what you had typed before showing history entries and brings it back when you come back down.

ai.title: Manicode README and package files export
ai.summary: Added manicode/README.md documenting CLI usage, knowledge.md context strategy, and installation. Updated manicode/package.json files field to export dist and README.md. This ensures the package contains necessary documentation and build artifacts when published.

eli5.text: The helper tool that runs from your command line now ships with a short guidebook inside its install package, so anyone who grabs it gets instructions on how to use it and how to keep a running notes file alongside their code. At the same time, two small spots inside the tool were taught to point to that guidebook and the ready-to-run version of the tool itself, so future copies of the tool include both the user directions and the working program files. Today, if you installed or downloaded this command-line assistant, you would see its README guide and the finished program files bundled together instead of one or both being left out.

ai.title: Add Manicode project structure knowledge base
ai.summary: New file `manicode/knowledge.md` documents the Manicode project structure, covering root configuration, source layout (`src/`), build process, and key components like `ChatClient` and `CLI`. This internal documentation establishes context for the AI agent's knowledge management system, detailing how `knowledge.md` files are used to store project-specific guidance. The file explicitly notes that Manicode is designed to update these knowledge files dynamically as it works.

eli5.text: The AI coding helper now has a new internal guidebook that explains how its own project is organized, so it can better understand where things live and how they fit together when it's working. This guidebook lives in a file called knowledge.md and describes the project's layout, the main building blocks that make up the tool, and how it's all put together. If you looked inside the project, you'd see this documentation file has been added; it also mentions that the AI is designed to keep updating these guidebooks as it learns more. This is behind-the-scenes documentation that helps the AI operate more effectively within its own system.

ai.title: Update manicode build process and tsconfig
ai.summary: Refactored `manicode/package.json` to chain `yarn build:common`, `yarn build:manicode`, and `yarn dist:copy` for the build script, replacing direct `tsc` invocation. Updated `manicode/tsconfig.json` to set `rootDir` to `./src` alongside `outDir`. This ensures proper compilation structure and artifact copying for the manicode package.

eli5.text: The build process for the Manicode package now runs three steps in order, building common code, building Manicode, and copying the results, instead of just running a compiler directly. The project also tells the compiler to read source files from a specific folder, which helps keep the output organized. If you watched the build run, you'd see it first finish shared code before compiling Manicode, then copy everything into a ready-to-use folder. This only matters to internal developers building or packaging Manicode; regular users won't notice anything different today.

ai.title: CLI chat response handling and storage fix
ai.summary: Fixed non-alternating chat bug by ensuring assistant messages are always persisted to ChatStorage, regardless of user stop requests. Refactored sendUserInputAndAwaitResponse to return a Promise resolving with response and file changes, replacing previous branching logic. Updated variable names (chartClient to chatClient, wsClient to client) in manicode/src/cli.ts and manicode/src/index.ts for consistency.

eli5.text: When you stop the assistant mid-reply, your conversation now stays properly ordered instead of leaving a gap that made follow-up messages look like they came from you. The assistant always saves its full answer to your chat history (including partial ones you cut off), then bundles that saved text together with any file changes it made, so the next turn lines up correctly. You would notice this if you watch your local chat history: assistant replies no longer disappear or appear out of sequence when you interrupt them, and the program behaves more predictably while you type and navigate past inputs. This fix is already live in the tool you run locally today.
